bull.t: Rapid AI connectivity adoption and platform expansion
bull.b: Strong adoption of PCIe 6 and the transition of Scorpio X into volume production show Astera is gaining content in increasingly complex AI servers. Broader connectivity requirements can support recurring platform demand, higher component content, and sustained revenue growth as hyperscale infrastructure expands.

The combination of high gross margins and substantial net profitability indicates differentiated semiconductor products with meaningful operating leverage. These economics give Astera capacity to fund research, product launches, and customer programs while retaining more cash as revenue scales.

bull.t: Debt-free balance sheet and strong liquidity
bull.b: A debt-free balance sheet and large cash position provide financial flexibility during product ramps and industry cycles. Astera can invest in roadmap expansion, support customer qualification efforts, and absorb execution variability without the interest burden or refinancing pressure associated with leverage.

bear.t: Scorpio ramp is concentrated among a few large programs
bear.b: Dependence on a small number of large Scorpio programs makes near-term results sensitive to customer timelines, qualification progress, and ramp execution. Until the customer base broadens, any delay or change in a major hyperscaler deployment could materially affect revenue growth and operating leverage.

bear.t: Profitability remains sensitive to product mix
bear.b: As Scorpio and module products become a larger share of sales, changes in lane count, use case, and customer mix can create meaningful margin variability. This sensitivity may limit the predictability of earnings conversion even while revenue grows and new products scale.

bear.t: Cash-flow consistency has not yet been established
bear.b: Recent cash generation is solid, but the year-over-year free-cash-flow decline and earlier negative periods show that reported profitability has not consistently translated into expanding cash. Working-capital movements or increased investment could continue to make funding capacity less predictable.
